name: lance_table::io::commit::external_manifest::finalize_staged
behavior: Public async finalize_staged<S: ExternalManifestStore + ?Sized> accepts an already selected staging path, version, expected size, raw object store and naming scheme. It computes the canonical manifest path, calls copy_or_verify_final_manifest, then constructs a canonical ManifestLocation with Some(size), the observed ETag and identity None. It does not itself acquire or validate the external reservation. Correct use requires the caller to have selected these immutable staging bytes. After the canonical copy succeeds, finalize_staged updates the existing external record to the canonical path/size with ETag None. Any index-update error is warned and swallowed: return the committed canonical location and retain staging for a later helper. Thus external index compaction is subsequent repair work, not rollback authority over the durable canonical object. A failed earlier copy/HEAD still propagates before this branch. Once index publication succeeds, finalize_staged deletes staging. Success and object-store NotFound proceed to a DELETE audit; any other delete failure warns and returns the canonical location without the audit. Cleanup failure cannot overturn commit. This helper does not update the version hint and has no cancellation guard spanning these awaits.

name: lance_table::io::commit::external_manifest::ExternalManifestStore::put
behavior: Default async put takes a selected-version candidate plus staging metadata and raw object-store handle. It deliberately ignores its ETag argument, calls put_if_not_exists with ETag None, and returns immediately on reservation error. Successful reservation proceeds to the overridable finalize hook; put itself contains no staging cleanup or retry. Atomic single-winner selection is a contract of the external implementation, not an in-process mutex here. Default put awaits finalize with the same base/version/path/size/store/scheme. Public async finalize delegates to finalize_staged; its documentation permits stores such as namespace-backed implementations to override publication. These hooks are separate from ExternalManifestCommitHandler's private reader finalizer, which directly runs the generic copy/repair protocol. A custom writer-side finalize override must therefore coordinate the form of locations returned to readers.

name: lance_table::io::commit::external_manifest::ExternalManifestStore::supports_predecessor_condition
behavior: supports_predecessor_condition defaults false; its contract requires supporting stores to populate ManifestLocation.identity. get_identity defaults Ok(None) and documents an immutable per-record incarnation token that is never reused. Support declaration alone does not enforce identity population, atomicity, retirement or listing behavior. Optional list_versions(base_uri, since) defaults Ok(None), selecting object-store fallback. A supported implementation returns all committed locations, optionally restricted to versions greater than since, carrying final paths and identities. This is required to discover predecessor-conditioned publications whose unique final filenames are invisible to ordinary manifest parsing; Some(empty) remains an authoritative empty history. Exact signatures are retained below. forget_version defaults to NotSupported and requires identity-conditional, idempotent removal when implemented; it differs from the parent CommitHandler default no-op. put_if_predecessor likewise defaults NotSupported and must atomically verify the supplied predecessor record identity and reserve the requested new version. This abstraction specifies a prerequisite record condition, not an enforced latest-version or adjacent-version check. Required put_if_not_exists and put_if_exists accept base URI, u64 version, path, u64 size and optional ETag; implementations receiving None must clear obsolete stored ETags. Generic workflow always supplies None. Optional delete defaults Ok(()) without action. Trait closure and spacing complete these extension boundaries; storage-specific atomic operations, schema and error mapping live in concrete implementations.

name: lance_table::io::commit::external_manifest::copy_via_read_rewrite
behavior: Private copy_via_read_rewrite opens the source GET stream before starting destination multipart upload, allocates a 100 MiB buffer and consumes stream chunks. A stream error attempts upload.abort, ignores abort failure and returns the original stream error. The function returns the object-store result type. Cancellation has no local Drop abort guard, so the explicit error branches do not cover all interrupted uploads. Each input chunk is sliced into the remaining part capacity and copied into the Vec. A full buffer is replaced with a fresh 100 MiB allocation, converted into Bytes and uploaded with a sequential awaited put_part; failure attempts abort and returns the original error. This bounds part buffers, not total memory: the current upstream chunk, in-flight payload and replacement allocation may coexist. Parts are not uploaded in parallel. A remaining nonempty buffer is uploaded as the short final part, with abort-on-error. Empty input proceeds to complete without a part. complete failure also attempts abort and preserves its original error; success returns Ok. No explicit total-byte comparison, checksum, part-count ceiling, abort-error reporting or cancellation cleanup is present; the caller's final HEAD checks only expected size.
